messages:
maria: FYI ran the overnight suite against p8-prod with the new allocator tweaks. Saw a cluster of OOMs around 03:12 UTC when prefixcache ttl=15m was enabled for canary.
dmitri: ugh. stacktrace or logs?
maria: pasted tail of the worker log: ```
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z ERROR oom: allocation failed 2.1GiB requested from workspace pool
model=redwood-7b variant=quantized kernel=flash_attn vram_left=1.2GiB
stack: runtime/allocator::alloc_workspace -> kvcache::prefetch -> inference::call
```
kai: interesting that vram_left was 1.2GiB. What was workspace sizing policy? did we change workspace_fraction?
maria: workspace_fraction=0.18 (per-GPU); workspace_soft_limit pinned to 1.6GiB for p8 flavor. only changed the kernel-routing heuristic yesterday to prefer fused-kernels for seq_len<=256.
dmitri: that lines up. fused kernel increases temporary buffer usage in some paths. Could push ephemeral allocations above the soft_limit and trigger OOM even if persistent caches fit.
elaine: before we jump, can we reproduce with a smaller harness? i can spin up a canary with TTL=15m and churn of prefixcache hits/evicts.
maria: yes, repro plan: synthetic load with 70% cache hit rate, random prompt length 60-512, batch sizes 1-6. I already have perf traces: perf-bot attached a flamegraph link -> https://perf.internal/runs/19912#flame
perf-bot: auto-attach: aggregated GPU mem alloc timeline + NVPROF snippets for run 19912.
kai: looking at the flamegraph, there's a big allocation spike in `kvcache::prefetch` immediately after `kernel_router::choose`. That suggests routing chose a kernel variant that forces a larger workspace. Kernel selection rule: prefer lower-latency kernel if (seq<=256 && batch<=4) else use streaming kernel.
dmitri: can we make routing aware of transient workspace pressure? e.g., add a metric `expected_workspace_delta` from kernel profiles and prefer the kernel with lower delta if free_vram<2GiB.
elaine: implementable. but we should be careful: sometimes lower-latency kernel yields higher throughput overall. Need guardrails: only override routing for requests that will likely allocate >1GiB extra.
maria: quick patch idea: compute `kernel_workspace_impact = max_kernel_workspace - kernel_persistent_footprint`. If free_vram < (kernel_workspace_impact + safety_margin) then route to fallback kernel. Safety_margin=512MiB.
kai: also need to consider KV cache prefetch windows. We saw prefetch brought in large KV chunks concurrently. Maybe limit concurrent prefetches per-GPU when vram_low.
dmitri: agree. Proposal: add adaptive prefetch gating: `max_concurrent_prefetch = base_prefetch * min(1, free_vram / vram_threshold)`. base_prefetch=8, vram_threshold=6GiB.
elaine: that's two levers: kernel routing and prefetch gating. Any perf regressions risk? We should run A/B on canary with telemetry for latency percentiles and token/sec.
maria: I ran a micro-A/B overnight with kernel-routing-change only. Results: p50 unchanged, p95 +7ms, p99 +18ms, but OOMs dropped from 6 -> 0 over 12h. Throughput unchanged.
kai: good trade for canary. But when we add prefetch gating we might hurt throughput on high-hit workloads.
dmitri: let's quantify. Can we run a grid of experiments varying: TTL {5m,15m,60m}, kernel-routing {old,adaptive}, prefetch_gate {off,adaptive}, workspace_fraction {0.14,0.18}? Run each for 1h synthetic traffic.
maria: I scheduled those. short report template I'll use: config, OOM_count, p50/p95/p99 latency delta vs baseline, tokens/sec, prefixcache_hitrate, evict_rate. Will upload to the experiments bucket.
elaine: question: should TTL=15m be default for canary? TTL affects footprint: shorter TTL reduces memory but increases misses and backend calls.
kai: for many production workloads, TTL=15m was ok because hit-rate stayed >80%. But our current canary saw oscillations when seq length distribution changes.
dmitri: another angle: defragmentation. The allocator fragmentation shows a lot of small free slabs between large pinned allocations. Could we opportunistically compact workspace allocations when prefetch is idle?
maria: compaction is heavier. There's a cheaper approach: ephemeral buffer reuse pool keyed by kernel variant + size class. That would reduce churn and peak.
kai: we've tried size-class pools for kernels before but struggled with concurrency. New idea: per-stream pool + per-GPU reserve. On stream idle, transfer small buffers back to reserve. Should be doable.
dmitri: combine that with adaptive max_concurrent_prefetch and kernel routing - should cut peak by ~0.7-1GiB in simulations.
maria: simulation today shows avg peak drop 840MiB with pools + gating, hit-rate unchanged. I'll push the perf traces and a small PR with flags `runtime.kernel_adaptive_routing`, `runtime.prefetch_gating`, `runtime.ephemeral_pool` behind feature flags.
deploy-bot: deploy request submitted: PR #4821 -> runtime: add adaptive routing + prefetch gating + ephemeral pool (flags off by default). CI: 22/23 green.
elaine: nice. next steps: 1) merge behind flags, 2) run full grid for 24h on canary, 3) review telemetry for regressions, 4) if safe, enable kernel_adaptive_routing for p8-prod only. I'll own rollout.
kai: one last ask: update model kernel profiles to include `workspace_impact_estimate` per seq_len bucket. That makes routing decisions more robust.
maria: noted. I'll export updated profiles as CSV -> s3://perf/profiles/kernel_workspace_199120.csv
dmitri: cool. If the canary proves stable, we can add a runtime metric `oom_risk_score` to alert earlier.
maria: added to the follow-up checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
